deckTitle: MedKayfab — Psychiatry Wrestling: The Mind-Bending Mat

cards.power: The Euphoria Spike. Too much in the mesolimbic track = Hallucinations. Too little in the mesocortical track = Flat affect.
cards.lore: Dino drives the Reward Road. Block him to stop the voices, but watch out for the Parkinsonian Rust.
cards.gradeReason: Great persona but lore is mechanistic; needs match context to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: retro wrestling card. Subject: ferocious T-Rex drooling gold coins in ring. Mood: manic reward frenzy.

cards.power: The Rhythm Keeper. Controls sleep, appetite, and the will to wrestle.
cards.lore: When Sally leaves the ring, the world turns grey. SSRIs act as vacuum plugs to keep her in the synaptic gap longer.
cards.gradeReason: Role clear, but text describes Sally's function more than what player embodies.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: colorful watercolor wrestling art. Subject: acrobatic lemur balancing mood, sleep, and hunger. Mood: rhythmic flow.

cards.power: The Big Chill. Tells the neurons to shut up and relax.
cards.lore: Benzodiazepines strengthen Garry's grip. A sudden withdrawal means brain on fire (seizures).
cards.gradeReason: Instant performative hook: walrus of calm. Player knows exactly what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Saturday morning cartoon brutalism. Subject: giant walrus slouched on CHILL sandbag radiating calm. Mood: sedated authority.

cards.power: The Spark. Gus is Garry's archnémesis. He turns on the lights and lets the sparks fly.
cards.lore: Too much Gus leads to excitotoxicity. Ketamine blocks Gus to perform a hard system reset.
cards.gradeReason: Archenemy framing with chaos energy is immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: explosive manga panel. Subject: electric squirrel hurling fireworks from open box. Mood: chaotic excitatory overload.

cards.power: The Delusion Bubble. Sam creates a reality where only he knows the rules.
cards.lore: Driven by Dino's rampage in the mesolimbic system. Requires at least 1 core symptom: delusion, hallucination, or disorganized speech.
cards.gradeReason: Delusion Bubble is strong but the diagnostic lore pulls out of performance mode.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surrealist wrestling poster. Subject: chameleon spinning in private reality bubble. Mood: paranoid otherworldly confidence.

cards.power: The Dual Threat. A dangerous mix of Sam's delusions and Barry's mood swings.
cards.lore: Sid is a border-crosser. He must prove his psychosis can exist even without the emotional roller coaster.
cards.gradeReason: Hybrid mechanic is clever but proof-of-psychosis lore reads as diagnostic rule.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: split-panel comic art. Subject: hyena wearing comedy and tragedy masks simultaneously, flames behind. Mood: volatile hybrid danger.

cards.power: The Snap. A sudden break with reality, usually after a traumatic match.
cards.lore: A temporary system failure. Berty returns completely to his old self after the match concludes.
cards.gradeReason: Time-limited psychosis creates instant dramatic tension; player knows the clock is ticking.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: kinetic action watercolor. Subject: shocked rabbit electrocuted by lightning, 1-month calendar crossed out. Mood: sudden catastrophic snap.

cards.power: The Unshakable Belief. Dan firmly believes the referee loves him or the FBI is hunting him.
cards.lore: Aside from his one quirk, Dan functions perfectly. He's not schizophrenic; he's just extremely stubborn.
cards.gradeReason: FBI-or-referee binary is comedy gold and instantly playable; best G1 hook in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda wrestling poster. Subject: determined bull pinning blank paper to brick wall labeled THE TRUTH. Mood: absolute unshakeable conviction.

cards.power: The Flight of Ideas. Builds a skyscraper ego in one night or feels like a crushed bug.
cards.lore: During mania, Barry needs no sleep and spends all his gold tokens. He thinks he is the invincible champion.
cards.gradeReason: Seesaw metaphor is visceral; manic-rainbow-dog vs crash is iconic and instantly embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic contrast illustration. Subject: rainbow dog blazing off seesaw into stars, other end buried in dirt. Mood: euphoric vertigo.

cards.power: The Gravity Well. Debbie makes every movement an ordeal. Even breathing feels like wrestling against lead.
cards.lore: Massive withdrawal of Sally and Nora. The world loses its color and value.
cards.gradeReason: Gravity Well is physically performable; grey tortoise under WORTHLESS GUILT boulder is devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: monochromatic watercolor. Subject: weeping tortoise crushed under boulder labeled WORTHLESS GUILT in storm clouds. Mood: suffocating grey weight.

cards.power: The Eternal Grey. Polly isn't as heavy as Debbie, but she never goes away.
cards.lore: A chronic state of not-quite-happiness. She is the rain that never stops.
cards.gradeReason: Excellent atmospheric card but a state rather than an action; needs table context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholy ink wash. Subject: frog in raincoat standing in puddle under endless drizzle. Mood: perpetual low-grade grey.

cards.power: The Constant Ripple. Cy is never stable, but his waves are small enough to stay out of the hospital.
cards.lore: The lite version of Barry. Most unstable character on the roster, but always stays in the ring.
cards.gradeReason: Mini-bipolar framing is clear but ripple power is descriptive rather than action-inviting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic kinetic sketch. Subject: meerkat on wobbly plank surrounded by small lightning bolts. Mood: low-amplitude perpetual instability.

cards.power: The Suffocator. Pete makes the heart race and the throat tighten with no opponent in the ring.
cards.lore: A false alarm from Norepi-Nora. Pete thinks he's dying even though he's just standing in a supermarket.
cards.gradeReason: No-opponent-in-the-ring is brilliant; supermarket death-fear is perfectly absurd and playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror comedy watercolor. Subject: puffed-up pufferfish hyperventilating alone in empty ring. Mood: escalating invisible terror.

cards.power: The Locker Room Lockdown. Abby fears places where she cannot escape quickly.
cards.lore: Often the result of Pete's attacks. Abby shrinks her world until only her house remains.
cards.gradeReason: World-shrinking is evocative but Abby is more reactive than performed; needs Pete on the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: claustrophobic pen-and-ink. Subject: armadillo curled in cardboard box inside empty wrestling ring. Mood: inescapable self-imprisonment.

cards.power: The Endless Reset. Otto must tie his shoes 50 times, otherwise the stadium will explode.
cards.lore: The action (compulsion) only serves to temporarily silence the agonizing thought (obsession).
cards.gradeReason: Stadium-explodes stakes make the ritual immediately performable; players get it instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: looping cartoon obsession. Subject: raccoon washing hands repeatedly while sneakers pile up and clock ticks. Mood: compelled frantic relief.

cards.power: The Time Warp. Paul is catapulted back into his worst match by a sound or a smell.
cards.lore: The brain has not archived the trauma. It remains an open wound that can tear again at any time.
cards.gradeReason: Trigger mechanic is vivid and dramatically immediate; time-warp-by-smell is perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fractured time panel art. Subject: wolf consumed by lightning flashback of past fight. Mood: involuntary violent memory intrusion.

cards.power: The Dopamine Handcuffs. Hali chains up the Dino and stops delusions immediately.
cards.lore: Effective but brutal. Causes EPS (extrapyramidal symptoms) — the wrestler becomes stiff as a statue.
cards.gradeReason: Dopamine Handcuffs is vivid but EPS-stiff-as-statue lore is more effect list than character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gritty cop drama wrestling. Subject: bulldog cop chaining miniature T-Rex in ring with heavy chain. Mood: brutal blunt force order.

cards.power: The Ultimate Override. The only one who wins when all other antipsychotics have failed.
cards.lore: She is the queen, but dangerous. Can eat white blood cells. For expert matches under supervision only!
cards.gradeReason: Last-resort queen who eats WBCs is immediately iconic and dramatically staged.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark gothic royalty. Subject: crowned lion queen with bloody sword standing over defeated white blood cells. Mood: supreme dangerous authority.

cards.power: The Prolactin Leak. Dampens psychosis but lets hormones go wild (gynecomastia/lactation).
cards.lore: Blocks dopamine and serotonin simultaneously. Modern approach with less rust than Hali.
cards.gradeReason: Prolactin Leak is memorably weird but the card is mechanism-forward rather than performance-forward.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mountain-peak adventure. Subject: armored goat tangling D2 and 5HT2A ropes on clifftop. Mood: nimble dual-receptor balancing act.

cards.power: The Metabolic Expansion. Stops voices but makes the wrestler twice as heavy within weeks.
cards.lore: Blocks histamine receptors, leading to insatiable hunger and insulin resistance.
cards.gradeReason: Twice-as-heavy-within-weeks is hilarious and instantly embodied; metabolic villain is legendary.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tragicomedy wrestling poster. Subject: enormous hippo sitting on flattened psychosis figure surrounded by fast food. Mood: effective but ruinous comfort.

cards.power: The Vacuum Plug. Plugs the drains so Sally can stay in the ring longer.
cards.lore: Needs 4-6 weeks to warm up. Side effect: the Sexual Snag (loss of libido).
cards.gradeReason: Sexual Snag is a memorable name but the card is more mechanism than performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: plumbing surrealism. Subject: beaver blocking drainage pipe while Sally floats on serotonin tide. Mood: slow-build careful chemistry.

cards.power: The Double Boost. Brings both Sally AND Nora back into the fight.
cards.lore: At high doses, Venny pushes blood pressure up. Good for Debbie when she has no energy left.
cards.gradeReason: Double Boost is clean but the card describes rather than invites performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: speed-blur action. Subject: cheetah in rocket suit blazing through storm carrying two flags. Mood: dual-neurotransmitter energy surge.

cards.power: The Dirty Bomb. Hits everything: serotonin, norepi, histamine, acetylcholine. Extremely effective but toxic in overdose.
cards.lore: The Old Guard. Unpopular due to anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation).
cards.gradeReason: Dirty Bomb firing into everything is instantly playable chaos; toxic overdose warning adds stakes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grunge punk explosion. Subject: armored rhino firing bazooka indiscriminately in ring explosion. Mood: brutal indiscriminate old-school power.

cards.power: The Forbidden Feast. Prevents breakdown of all transmitters. Warning: no cheese, no wine!
cards.lore: Tyramine danger! If Mao blocks tyramine breakdown, blood pressure explodes (hypertensive crisis).
cards.gradeReason: No-cheese-no-wine is theatrical gold; tyramine crisis adds genuine dramatic danger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sinister feast illustration. Subject: vulture in cloak guarding FORBIDDEN cheese-and-wine table. Mood: dangerous power with deadly dietary rules.

cards.power: The Suicidal Shield. The only one who can truly anchor Barry's seesaw to the ground.
cards.lore: Lou hates the thyroid and kidneys. Narrow therapeutic window — too much Lou is pure poison.
cards.gradeReason: Suicidal Shield with narrow-window-poison is instantly dramatic; anchor imagery is visceral.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: maritime drama. Subject: pelican chained to giant anchor on seesaw, kidney weeping nearby. Mood: stabilizing but treacherous equilibrium.

cards.power: The Mania Muzzler. Helps Garry calm the ring down. Especially good for mixed states.
cards.lore: Absolute ban for pregnant wrestlers! Causes hair loss and weight gain.
cards.gradeReason: Mania Muzzler is a good image but side effects list reads as reference rather than theatre.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bear wrestling drama. Subject: giant bear muzzling manic kangaroo under colorful blanket. Mood: potent but teratogenically dangerous calm.

cards.power: The Instant Off-Switch. When Pete panics or Barry riots, Lora sends them to sleep immediately.
cards.lore: High addiction potential! Like a loan — solves the problem now, but you pay with interest (withdrawal).
cards.gradeReason: Loan metaphor is perfect; sends opponents to sleep on contact with withdrawal debt attached.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir bouncer drama. Subject: weasel in suit firing sedative pistol at panicking pill characters. Mood: instant decisive knockout with debt clause.

cards.power: The Smooth Landing. Used to bring wrestlers safely through alcohol withdrawal.
cards.lore: Because of the long action, Diaz accumulates in the body. He is the marathon runner of benzos.
cards.gradeReason: Marathon runner is good but Diaz is defined more by what he outlasts than what he performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: lazy sky adventure. Subject: sloth parachuting in slow motion above wrestling ring. Mood: long-acting smooth deceleration.

cards.power: The Conspiracy Theory. Thinks everyone in the crowd and his partner wants to betray him.
cards.lore: Not psychotic; just extremely suspicious. Reads hostile intent into harmless comments.
cards.gradeReason: Cluster A spy persona is instantly playable; not-psychotic distinction is clinically crisp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: detective noir. Subject: ostrich in trench coat magnifying-glassing bewildered bear. Mood: constant background betrayal suspicion.

cards.power: The Void of Interest. Wants no friends, no dates, no fans. Prefers wrestling in an empty stadium.
cards.lore: Isn't shy — he just doesn't care. Considers neither praise nor criticism important.
cards.gradeReason: Empty-stadium preference is the single best behavioral detail in the deck; instantly embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: solitary minimalism. Subject: owl meditating in empty spotlight ring, all seats dark. Mood: complete affectless voluntary isolation.

cards.power: The Strange Vibe. Wears odd clothes and claims he can read the thoughts of the ring posts.
cards.lore: Sam's eccentric cousin. No hallucinations, but his reality is very... specific.
cards.gradeReason: Ring-post telepathy is immediately embodied; Shaman persona gives rich performance space.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychedelic shaman art. Subject: peacock in robes holding skull reading runes off wrestling post. Mood: eccentric magical certainty.

cards.power: The Social Detachment.
cards.lore: The weird group. Paranoia, isolation, and eccentricity define this wrestling stable.
cards.gradeReason: Stub power; reference card with no performative hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: group lineup poster. Subject: ostrich, owl, peacock trio in locker room looking weird together. Mood: eccentric antisocial solidarity.

cards.power: The Rule Breaker. Strikes when the ref isn't looking. Feels no remorse and loves risk.
cards.lore: Before age 15, called Conduct Disorder Charlie. Has no respect for the laws of the ring.
cards.gradeReason: Wrestling Heel is the perfect vessel for ASPD; strikes-when-ref-isn't-looking is instantly performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: villain wrestling poster. Subject: fox punching from behind while referee looks away, crowd shocked. Mood: gleeful remorseless rule violation.

cards.power: The Splitting Move. Today you are Bella's hero; tomorrow her worst enemy. Nothing in between.
cards.lore: Massive fear of abandonment. Uses self-harm to dampen the inner pain.
cards.gradeReason: Hero-to-worst-enemy flip is a dramatic mechanic players can run with immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: shattered mirror drama. Subject: hedgehog hugging heart and smashing mirror simultaneously. Mood: volatile love-hate with no grey zone.

cards.power: The Spotlight Stealer. Cries, screams, or undresses — as long as all cameras are on her.
cards.lore: Her feelings are like stage props: loud, colorful, but shallow. Needs validation like oxygen.
cards.gradeReason: Three-way or-action (cries/screams/undresses) gives player immediate expressive options.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: showbiz excess. Subject: flamingo in sequined dress wailing into microphone as cameras swarm. Mood: maximal theatrical attention demand.

cards.power: The Mirror Worship. Convinced he is the only true champion. Everyone else is an extra.
cards.lore: Under his giant ego hides a tiny self-esteem that breaks at the slightest criticism.
cards.gradeReason: Everyone-else-is-an-extra plus hidden tiny self-esteem is psychologically perfect and playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: golden grandiosity. Subject: lion punching rival while admiring himself in gilded mirror. Mood: fragile ego wrapped in unstoppable bravado.

cards.power: The Rejection Fear. Would love to join in, but convinced everyone will laugh at her.
cards.lore: Unlike Sid, Ava WANTS closeness, but her inferiority complexes keep her in the locker room.
cards.gradeReason: Wants-closeness distinction from Sid is clinically sharp but card describes state not action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: shy watercolor. Subject: mouse peeking from behind curtain at empty ring she desperately wants to enter. Mood: longing paralyzed by rejection fear.

cards.power: The Decision Trap. Can't even choose which boots to wear without asking her coach.
cards.lore: Needs someone to take responsibility for her life. Alone, she feels completely helpless.
cards.gradeReason: Boots detail is funny but the card describes incapacity rather than inviting performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: clinging comedy. Subject: koala latched onto bear coach unable to step toward ring alone. Mood: paralytic dependency disguised as affection.

cards.power: The Checklist Attack. Spends the whole match ironing the ropes and disinfecting the mat.
cards.lore: Unlike OCD, Oliver LIKES his control obsession. He thinks everyone else is just sloppy.
cards.gradeReason: Ironing-the-ropes-during-a-match is theatrical genius; LIKES-his-obsession distinction is crisp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: perfectionist comedy. Subject: badger ironing ring ropes with spirit level while opponent waits baffled. Mood: smug perfectionist self-righteousness.

cards.power: The Inhibition.
cards.lore: The worried group. Fear, uncertainty, and perfectionism prevent free combat.
cards.gradeReason: Stub power; reference card with no performative hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anxious bench scene. Subject: mouse, koala, badger huddled anxiously on locker room bench. Mood: collective paralysis of the worried stable.

cards.power: The DT-Shake. When Al runs out of juice, the ring shakes. Confusion, fever, hallucinations.
cards.lore: Alcohol withdrawal is the most dangerous. Without Garny (GABA), the brain goes haywire.
cards.gradeReason: DT timeline stat is clinically perfect and theatrically vivid; ring-shakes is immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: delirium tremens horror watercolor. Subject: grizzly bear hallucinating pink elephants in purple ring. Mood: sweating fever-dream collapse.

cards.power: The Slow Motion. Feels no more pain, but barely breathes. Drifts away.
cards.lore: Blocks pain signals in the spinal cord and dampens the respiratory center in the brainstem.
cards.gradeReason: The Nod is iconic; barely-breathes-drifts-away gives player precise physical performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dreamy narcoleptic illustration. Subject: basset hound in wrestling gear half-asleep mid-sway with zzz clouds. Mood: painless respiratory slow fade.

cards.power: The Instant Wake-Up. Kicks the door down and throws Ollie off the receptors immediately.
cards.lore: Saves lives but triggers brutal, instant withdrawal. The wrestler wakes up screaming and vomiting.
cards.gradeReason: Door-kicking reversal with screaming-vomiting consequence is dramatically perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: emergency action comic. Subject: kangaroo in scrubs throwing ice bucket at collapsed basset hound. Mood: life-saving violence with brutal awakening.

cards.power: The Heart Race. Infinite energy but makes the wrestler paranoid and aggressive.
cards.lore: Warning: Never give beta-blockers! Leads to an unopposed alpha strike — blood pressure shoots through the roof.
cards.gradeReason: Infinite-energy-plus-paranoid is playable immediately; beta-blocker danger adds lethal stakes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: electric paranoia explosion. Subject: electric fox in ring blazing with lightning, pupils wide, fists flying. Mood: manic aggressive stimulant overload.

cards.power: The Black & White Vision. Divides the world into heroes and traitors. No grey zone.
cards.lore: A primitive defense to reduce the complexity of feelings.
cards.gradeReason: Heroes-and-traitors binary is clear but as a defense mechanism needs Bella on table to activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: stark black-and-white. Subject: giant spider splitting ring into pure white hero zone and pure black traitor zone. Mood: binary primitive defense.

cards.power: The Mirror Toss. Throws his own unacceptable impulses onto his opponent.
cards.lore: Protects his ego by searching for and fighting his own faults in others.
cards.gradeReason: Mirror Toss is clever but the defense mechanism meta-layer needs context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: accusatory portrait. Subject: baboon pointing furiously at own reflection in mirror blaming the monkey. Mood: displaced self-hatred projected outward.

cards.power: The Angry Slide. Takes out his frustration on someone weaker or blameless.
cards.lore: Rage is shifted from the dangerous source to a safe target.
cards.gradeReason: Boss-to-locker example is relatable but text is explanatory rather than action-inviting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: frustrated action cartoon. Subject: ram charging teddy bear with rage-redirect arrow from boss. Mood: cowardly displaced aggression.

cards.power: The Rage Reform. Transforms her aggression into training and mastery.
cards.lore: The only healthy way. Dark energy is used for something good.
cards.gradeReason: Only-healthy-way framing is conceptually strong but less performance-urgent than primitive defenses.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tiger training poster. Subject: tiger in boxing gloves channeling flames into punching bag. Mood: controlled dark energy transformed into mastery.

cards.power: The Squirrel Chase. Cannot focus on his opponent because a butterfly is flying by.
cards.lore: Stimulants (methylphenidate) help switch his filter system back on.
cards.gradeReason: Butterfly-in-ring is theatrical perfection; Squirrel Chase is immediately performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: distracted action comedy. Subject: golden retriever wrestler chasing butterfly while opponent lies forgotten. Mood: joyful total attentional collapse.

cards.power: The Mirror Lie. Sees a giant in the mirror, though she's just skin and bones.
cards.lore: Danger: refeeding syndrome! If she eats after a long time, phosphate drops and the heart fails.
cards.gradeReason: Mirror Lie is powerful but pivots to clinical warning; emotional core competes with safety info.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: distorted mirror drama. Subject: skeletal greyhound seeing obese pug in hospital mirror. Mood: tragic dysmorphic self-deception.

cards.power: The Rigor Mortis Attack. Makes muscles as hard as iron bars. Life-threatening emergency!
cards.lore: Violent reaction to D2 blockers (Hali). Therapy: stop med, cool down, give dantrolene.
cards.gradeReason: Emergency card with vivid imagery but treatment protocol lore is reference not theatre.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: red-alert emergency. Subject: stone rhino crackling with heat lines in danger-stripe ring. Mood: life-threatening rigid crisis.

cards.power: The Shiver Shake. Too much Sally in the soup. Legs tremble uncontrollably (clonus).
cards.lore: Combo of SSRIs and MAOIs. Muscles over-cranked but not rigid like Mel's.
cards.gradeReason: Clonus-as-shiver is clear but comparison-to-Mel framing makes card self-referential.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: electric red danger. Subject: red jellyfish convulsing in boxing gloves in ring. Mood: serotonin overload trembling emergency.

cards.power: The Risk Check. Before the match begins, must check: Is the wrestler a danger to himself?
cards.lore: If the Sentry says YES, the fight ends immediately — safety first!
cards.gradeReason: Gatekeeper function is clear and serious; role is procedural rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: guardian drama. Subject: gorilla holding SAD PERSONS shield blocking ring entrance. Mood: protective solemn pre-match safety check.

cards.power: The Memory Eraser. Walt is the emergency (give thiamine!); Ken is the lasting damage (invents stories).
cards.lore: Without vitamin B1, the brain dies. Ken doesn't lie intentionally — he just fills the holes.
cards.gradeReason: Split card is conceptually rich but dual-character structure needs explanation before play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tragic duo portrait. Subject: confused parrot with colander hat and glazed memory-erased eyes. Mood: acute emergency fading into permanent confabulation.

cards.power: The Systemic Diagnosis.
cards.lore: Is it organic or psychiatric? Rule out the body before you blame the mind. Gestalt is dead. Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Stay-fluffy sign-off lands; Gestalt-is-dead is sharp — but stub power limits performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: boss reveal spotlight. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit in lab coat with magnifying glass, one giant eye scanning ring. Mood: systematic diagnostic authority.

cards.power: Identify NMS-Mel (Lead-Pipe Fever), Diagnose Al-the-Alcoholic (48-Hour Shakes), Call Narcan-Nancy (Heroin Nod).
cards.lore: MedKayfab Psychiatry Edition v1.0 complete. Mind the gap!
cards.gradeReason: Scenario/quest card; no character or roleplay hook — pure clinical application reference.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: quest scroll comic. Subject: ancient parchment with tiny wrestlers enacting three emergency scenarios. Mood: clinical synthesis challenge scroll.

verdict: One of the strongest MedKayfab decks in the roster — 56 cards covering the full psychiatric breadth from neurotransmitters to emergency syndromes with consistently vivid wrestling personas. Delusional Dan, Mao the MAOI, OCPD-Oliver, and Schizoid Sid are top-tier cards that will be quoted at tables. The Panic-Pete POWER duplication bug and the Schizoaffective Sid / Schizoid Sid name collision are the only meaningful defects in an otherwise excellent deck. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: The complete psychiatric roster in one wild wrestling card deck — from Dopamine-Dino to Mao the MAOI. For med students, psych nurses, and anyone who needs to know why you never give beta-blockers to Cokie.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob wrestling doctor holds flaming DSM-5 in chaotic neuron ring; fully loaded visual.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Psychiatry Wrestling: The Mind-Bending Mat' is punchy, thematic, and brand-perfect.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Wrestling plus psychiatry synthesis is the MedKayfabe brand in pure form.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — No other psychiatry education product looks like this.
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — High shareability but complex composition may compress poorly at small size.
coverQA.coverNote: Strong contender for best MedKayfab cover. The flaming DSM-5, placebo alien, and neuron ring together communicate the entire deck premise in one image. 'It's not a chemical imbalance, it's a tactical glitch' is quotable gold.

notes: Page 5 Panic-Pete layout bug: POWER block duplicated twice (both identical), LORE block visible below — recorded single POWER instance. Two 'Sid' characters: Schizoaffective Sid (p3) and Schizoid Sid (p9) — different conditions, identical first name, potential table confusion. 'Nora' (Norepinephrine) referenced in cards 10, 13, 22 but has no standalone card in this deck. Cluster B has no Summary card; Clusters A and C do — structural asymmetry. Page 9 Schizotypal Skip has decorative micro-text background marginalia (Sergio Aragonés-style), not card content.
